the use of the terms SJS and TEN are interchangeable and should not be used separately.
the most important factor in preventing Stevens-Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis is to stop taking the offending medication and to seek medical attention immediately.

there is no evidence to support the use of any specific treatment modality, including corticosteroid, cyclosporine, intravenous immunoglobulin or plasmapheresis, to prevent or reduce the severity of the mucocutaneous lesions of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS), Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN), or the associated extracutaneous manifestations, and that the use of these agents in these settings is not supported by the current literature.
